streak_assessment: Six consecutive scientific non-improvements since the exp-0089 promotion: exp-0090 king-danger 0.508, exp-0091 passed pawns 0.531, exp-0092 rook-open-file 0.492, exp-0093 pawn structure 0.484, exp-0094 in-tree repetition scoring 0.531, exp-0095 lone-king mop-up 0.461 (CI [0.390, 0.533]). The numeric half of the stop rule (>=5) is well exceeded, and the search / move-ordering / quiescence / time-management family and the middlegame positional-scalar family are both saturated. The stop rule also requires that no materially different, well-motivated experiment remains. One does. Every experiment in the window has either changed search mechanics or added a hand-weighted positional scalar that perturbs positions the trained model already handles; none has addressed the fact that the trained piece-square model has no move-counter input at all, so a winning position on move 2 of a plan and the same winning position on move 20 of aimless shuffling are literally indistinguishable to the leaf evaluation, and no amount of search depth supplies a gradient that is absent from the leaf. exp-0095 did not disprove endgame-conversion evaluation: its gate (exactly one side has mating material, the other is a bare king) fired in approximately zero of the 64 arena games (1 insufficient-material draw vs 32 repetition draws that still had pieces on both sides), so its neutral result reflects an untriggered mechanism, not a refuted hypothesis. A halfmove-clock progress gradient fires in every reduced-material endgame regardless of piece configuration and is the minimal closed-form fix for the dominant failure. CONTINUE for one more experiment; if it is inconclusive, the next audit should declare scientific_saturation and escalate an offline retrain.
recurring_failure_modes: Threefold-repetition draws dominate outcomes: 32 of 33 draws in exp-0095, a large share from equal or materially winning positions, with the engine shuffling a king or piece because nothing in the leaf evaluation rewards progress; entire opening pairs (open-game, english, reti, caro-kann, kings-indian, pirc, dutch, nimzo-indian, slav, french) drawn by repetition with both colours.

Every decisive loss (18 of 18) is a checkmate, skewed toward the candidate as White, delivered by a long king hunt after the engine trades pieces into a simplified position with an exposed king and no counterplay.

Root cause: the leaf evaluation (tapered PST model + 3 cp/square net mobility + flat castling scalar) has no notion of the 50-move counter or of making progress; PST values are identical for a shuffled king/piece and the mobility term is near zero in cramped or simplified positions, so alpha-beta values a winning-but-shuffling position as static no matter how deep it searches.

Hand-weighted middlegame positional scalars (king danger exp-0090, passed pawns exp-0091, rook files exp-0092, pawn structure exp-0093) all washed out because they only perturb positions the trained model already evaluates competently and do not touch the shuffling behaviour that produces the draws.

Mate-distance and repetition-value mechanisms are spent: draw contempt (exp-0063) only re-values an already-recognised draw and gives no direction; in-tree repetition scoring (exp-0094) is a search-tree value change that needs the repetition already present; mate-distance scoring acts only after a mate is found in-tree, and the relevant mates are 15-25 plies beyond the horizon.

next_direction.title: Halfmove-clock progress gradient in the leaf evaluation for reduced-material endgames
next_direction.hypothesis: In agent.py's _model_evaluate, fold a cheap side-relative non-king material total into the existing piece loop (accumulate material_diff += sign * SEE_VALUES[piece_type] * len(squares) for piece_type != chess.KING, reusing the squares list and sign already computed). After the midgame/endgame blend and the existing mobility/castling terms, apply a bounded progress gradient gated to reduced-material, materially decided endgames: if phase <= 10 (both sides reduced to roughly a queen, or a rook plus a minor, or less) AND abs(material_diff) >= 300 (at least a clean minor-piece advantage for one side), compute pull = min(board.halfmove_clock, 80) * 0.35 and do score -= math.copysign(pull, material_diff). This penalises the side that is ahead for a rising 50-move counter (maximum about 28 model units, below a pawn and far below any mate score, so it can only break ties and can never invert a position material already calls won or lost), giving alpha-beta a monotone reason to prefer clock-resetting pawn moves, captures and trades over the king/piece shuffling that currently produces 32 of 33 draws by threefold repetition; and symmetrically it rewards the side that is behind for a rising counter, giving the engine a reason to steer lost endgames toward the 50-move draw rather than into the long king hunts that account for all 18 decisive losses. No change to _ordered_moves, _quiescence, _negamax, the transposition-table key or size, _forced_draw, _budget_seconds, the iterative-deepening loop, MATE handling, or weights/.
next_direction.rationale: The dominant retained failure across six straight experiments is non-forced threefold-repetition draws, many from winning or equal positions, plus a loss column that is entirely checkmates after passive simplification. The mechanical cause is specific and untouched: the trained piece-square model has no move-counter feature, its PST is identical for a king or piece shuffled between two squares, and the accepted mobility term (exp-0089) is near zero for a lone or cramped king, so the leaf evaluation cannot distinguish steady progress from aimless shuffling in a technically winning position, and a missing gradient cannot be recovered by searching deeper because the converting mate is 15-25 plies past the horizon. A halfmove-clock term is the minimal closed-form way to inject that gradient. It is materially different from every exhausted mechanism: draw contempt (exp-0063) only re-values an already-recognised draw and supplies no direction toward the win; in-tree repetition scoring (exp-0094) changes a search-tree value and needs the repetition already on the board or in the line; mate-distance scoring acts only once a mate is found in-tree; and exp-0095's coordinate mop-up term was gated to bare-king endings that fired in essentially none of the 64 arena games, so it left endgame-conversion evaluation genuinely untested rather than refuted. A clock gradient fires in every reduced-material endgame regardless of piece configuration (queen, rook, rook-versus-minor, king-and-pawn races) and directly rewards the concrete progress moves the engine currently declines. It keeps the trained model fully determinative of every middlegame and every non-reduced endgame, and of every model-move-ablation opening, and it is a roughly ten-line self-contained change with four hand-chosen scalars, no coefficient from training and no weights change.
next_direction.guardrails: Scope: edit only agent.py; weights/ untouched; no change to _ordered_moves, _quiescence, _negamax, the TT key or size, _forced_draw, _budget_seconds, or the iterative-deepening loop. NPS / leaf cost: the material accumulator must be a single multiply-add folded into the existing board.pieces loop, and the post-loop block is about four integer comparisons plus one math.copysign when the gate passes and near-nothing when it fails (virtually every middlegame node and every model-ablation node); target node cost within 1.02x and confirm the paired arena reaches search depth comparable to exp-0095. Correctness bound: hard-cap the contribution at min(halfmove_clock, 80) * 0.35, about 28 model units, so it can only break ties among equal-material shuffle positions and can never flip the sign of a position material evaluation already calls winning or losing; require abs(material_diff) >= 300 so the term never fires in materially level endings or in single-pawn endings such as K+P versus K or R+P versus R where rushing to reset the clock is often the wrong idea and a draw may be correct; require phase <= 10 so the term is completely inert in the middlegame. Model-move-ablation safety: the 3 s ablation openings start from standard opening positions and effectively never reach a phase <= 10, >= 300 cp endgame, so the term is inert on that path; require model_move_ablation to still pass with minimum_differences >= 8 and the observed differences materially unchanged from exp-0095's 28 of 32, and confirm the arena strength gate is not regressed. Reliability / flag risk: no new hot-path work, so re-verify the full stress_time_left_ms grid (1 / 25 / 100 / 1000 / 120000 ms) with required_failures 0 and init under 50 s; exp-0095's worst single move was 0.87 s against the 2.25 s ceiling and 0.0002 s against 0.75 s at the 1 ms clock, and this change adds no measurable work, so that margin must be preserved. CI, ruff, mypy, smoke, resource and policy gates must stay green with zero agent failures. Anti-tuning: if the paired arena is inconclusive, do NOT re-run this by adjusting the 0.35, 80, 300 or phase-cap constants, by making the term asymmetric, by switching from halfmove_clock to a ply count, or by adding a second clock-derived term and calling it a new experiment; that outcome is the seventh consecutive non-improvement and the next audit should declare stop_condition scientific_saturation and hand the human an offline retrain of weights/model.json with trained positional and endgame features (king activity, pawn structure, passed pawns, and a tempo/progress signal), since every self-contained hand-weighted leaf option will then be exhausted.

audit_summary: Champion is agent.py at commit 4a0c988 (recorded as exp-0089): PVS/LMR negamax with exchange-aware capture ordering and losing-capture pruning in a depth-3 quiescence, a depth-keyed transposition table on (transposition_key, halfmove_clock, depth), partial root-iteration salvage, and a fast draw path (_forced_draw = halfmove_clock>=100 OR is_repetition(3) OR insufficient material), over a tapered learned piece-square model plus an accepted fixed 3 cp/square net-mobility leaf term and a flat castling-rights scalar. The batch just completed produced exp-0095, the previous audit's chosen direction: a bounded coordinate-based mop-up king-drive term added to _model_evaluate, gated strictly to won lone-king endgames and hard-capped at 60 units. It returned an inconclusive sequential paired arena (13 wins, 33 draws, 18 losses, score 0.461, CI [0.390, 0.533]) with CI, model-move ablation (28 of 32 move differences, minimum 8), reliability stress (init 0.22 s, worst move 0.87 s vs the 2.25 s ceiling), resources (peak 120 MB vs 2 GB), ruff, mypy, smoke and policy gates all green and zero agent failures; not promoted, so the mop-up term is not in the champion. This is the sixth consecutive scientific non-improvement since exp-0089 (exp-0090 0.508, exp-0091 0.531, exp-0092 0.492, exp-0093 0.484, exp-0094 0.531, exp-0095 0.461), so the numeric half of the stop rule is met and the search/ordering/quiescence/time family and the middlegame positional-scalar family are both saturated. exp-0095's retained games show the failure modes unchanged: 32 of 64 draws by threefold repetition, many from winning or equal positions with aimless shuffling, whole opening pairs (open-game, english, reti, caro-kann, kings-indian, pirc, dutch, nimzo-indian, slav, french) drawn by both colours; and all 18 losses are checkmates by long king hunts after passive simplification, skewed toward the candidate as White. Critically, exp-0095's gate (one side has mating material, the other is a bare king) fired in essentially none of the 64 games (1 insufficient-material draw versus 32 repetition draws that still had pieces on both sides), so its neutral result reflects an untriggered mechanism rather than a refuted hypothesis. Decision: CONTINUE, stop_condition null, because one materially different, well-motivated, self-contained experiment remains that no record in the window has tried and that targets the dominant failure at its mechanical cause: a bounded halfmove-clock progress gradient in _model_evaluate, gated to reduced-material endgames (phase <= 10) with a clean material edge (>= 300 cp), that penalises the winning side for a rising 50-move counter and symmetrically rewards the losing side, hard-capped near 28 units, well below a pawn. The trained piece-square model has no move-counter feature and identical PST for shuffled positions, so the shuffle-versus-progress distinction is invisible to the leaf evaluation and unreachable by deeper search; this term is the minimal closed-form fix. It is distinct from draw contempt (exp-0063, which only re-values a recognised draw and gives no direction), from in-tree repetition scoring (exp-0094, a search-value change that needs the repetition already present), from mate-distance scoring (acts only after a mate is found in-tree), and from the exp-0095 mop-up term (lone-king only). It keeps the trained model determinative of every middlegame and every non-reduced endgame and every ablation opening, adds negligible node cost behind a gate that piggybacks on the existing piece loop, and touches no protected surface, no weights, no time management and no TT structure. This is the last self-contained evaluation idea: if exp-0096 is inconclusive the next audit should declare scientific_saturation and escalate an offline positional/endgame-feature retrain of weights/model.json to the human. Uploading remains out of scope; the live submission is v3 (artifact sha prefix 55fec84c6dab, state.json status active) tied to the exp-0089 champion, and this audit does not touch it.
